$comment: Kit register (scripts/formal). Complements formal/claims.json, which stays the full inventory read by scripts/check-claims.py; each claim here names its legacy claim in $comment. See docs/dev/FORMAL.md.

claims.statement: On the fixed corpus in formal/oracle, the Rust signing and hashing preimages (authority evidence, hiding commitment, record body, record content hash pin, taxonomy tag) equal the bytes of the executable Lean model, and every signed-tag literal in the Rust sources has a Lean preimage family.
claims.detector: cargo test -q -p averin-decision-core --test oracle && python3 formal/check-refinement.py
claims.does_not_establish: Agreement outside the committed corpus and tag inventory. It is sampled conformance, not a refinement proof (the proved seal path is production-seal-refinement in formal/claims.json). It does not show the Lean model expresses the intended format, and says nothing about signatures, keys or the verifier's decisions.

claims.statement: The v3 authority signature preimage includes the semantic subject digest, checked against the committed govder cross-plane vector.
claims.does_not_establish: That the subject projection covers every semantic field (reviewed by hand when the record schema changes), the recorder-authenticated exclusions, or that the authority approved the subject. One vector, not all records.

claims.statement: The Rust claim kernel (capstone, revocation readiness and historical claim conditions) returns the same decision as the Lean verdict model on the committed exhaustive and named evidence-state corpus.
claims.does_not_establish: Evidence states outside the corpus, or that verify.rs computes the facts the kernel consumes (the proved refinement in formal/claims.json covers the kernel only, and the fact computation is tested, not proved).

claims.statement: The adversarial suite pins the temporal revocation decisions: a receipt at the cutoff ordinal is not before it, an ordinal beyond the snapshot watermark is indeterminate, an over-age snapshot is stale, a Merkle v2 leaf commits mode and cutoff, and a cutoff above the watermark is rejected.
claims.does_not_establish: Behaviour on inputs the tests do not construct. This is example-based testing, not a proof of temporal ordering, and it assumes the snapshot and revocation issuer are authentic (pinned out of band).

claims.statement: A failed proof-of-possession on a two-phase intent stays a violation under checkpoint-anchor stripping and does not consume its outcome, and required disclosure must cover every committed broker grant.
claims.does_not_establish: Any bundle shape the adversarial suite does not build. Example-based tests, not a proof of monotonicity under deletion (the Lean model states that; its production kernel refinement does not cover verify.rs fact computation).

claims.statement: A textual gate fails when production code stops calling the extracted and proved seal and verdict functions, or when a feature flag or cfg could select different hashing code.
claims.does_not_establish: That the extracted code is correct (that is the Lean proof run in formal-production), or anything beyond the call sites and cfg forms the script scans. It is a textual check, not a semantic one.

claims.statement: The RCP parser matches the reference parser on a generated corpus and survives a seeded deterministic fuzz campaign without panic, including truncated escapes, truncated literals, long digit strings and trailing whitespace.
claims.does_not_establish: Totality for all inputs (the Lean parser-totality proof in formal/claims.json is the stronger evidence; this checks sampled inputs only). Not input that is not valid UTF-8: both tests pass Rust strings, so a truncated UTF-8 sequence never reaches the parser here (mutant m60 survives these tests; only the totality proof kills it). Not allocation failure, stack depth or the uncapped options JSON path.

claims.statement: Within each harness's stated bounds, Kani checks the real LP framing (4-byte big-endian length) and base64url tail canonicality for two- and three-symbol tails.
claims.does_not_establish: Anything outside the harness bounds. It does not cover the other harnesses of bounded-real-encoders in formal/claims.json (UTF-16 key order, strict decoder, integer and string families), which need Kani proof stubs and are mutation-tested by the legacy suite only. Kani 0.68.0 and CBMC are trusted. A failing detector here does not tell an unwinding failure from a real counterexample; formal/check-kani-mutant.py in the legacy mutation suite makes that distinction.

claims.statement: The Lean hand model builds with warnings as errors and every Averin declaration depends only on the standard axioms; the record seal theorems need the stated format-injectivity hypothesis and conclude equal bodies or an explicit SHA-256 collision.
claims.does_not_establish: That the Lean model matches the Rust (see preimage-oracle-conformance and the extraction-based claims in formal/claims.json). Model-level only: SHA-256 collision resistance, Ed25519 unforgeability, an honest signer and post-NFC inputs are assumptions, and the Lean kernel is trusted.

claims.statement: Within the finite constants of the configurations (two replicas), TLC finds no violation of NoFrontierFork, NoCheckpointFork and NoStaleCheckpoint in ProjectTx_safe.cfg, and the witness configurations (unserialized, checkpoint_fork, stale_cache, pending_cache) still produce their expected counterexamples, so the model keeps showing the bugs the serialization guard is there to prevent.
claims.does_not_establish: Model-level only: it is not bound to the Go or Postgres code. The bounds are finite (two replicas, small constants), so it says nothing about larger configurations. ProjectTx_operational_safe.cfg holds by definition (Authoritative = TRUE makes badUse and badFinalize unreachable) and is not counted as evidence. GrantLog.tla and ConsumeLedger.tla model superseded designs and are not registered. TLC and the Java runtime are trusted.

claims.statement: record::seal returns Ok only for a body whose sealed form passes verify_sealed's top-level shape check, domain pin and canon_version pin, so a record that every verifier rejects on those grounds cannot be sealed through record::seal (SB-29). Held as a deterministic property test over every single defect (unknown key, each dropped required key, wrong or non-string or missing domain, wrong canon_version) plus 600 seeded random defect combinations on the golden record body, and, on the Go side, by running the whole server test suite through the real cgo seal in enforce mode and failing the run if any producer kind is refused or no longer reached.
claims.does_not_establish: Nothing about nested object shape (validate_record_shape checks top-level keys only; the JSON Schema covers the rest), content_hash or signature validity of a body, or any record sealed before this change. Not a proof: the generator is deterministic and finite, so a defect class it does not build is untested. The Go conformance covers only the producers the existing server tests reach, and a body type no test builds is checked only by the seal refusing it at runtime. Nothing about checkpoints: checkpoint::seal_checkpoint still does not pin the checkpoint domain or canon_version (verify_checkpoint_sealed does). AVERIN_SEAL_SHAPE=shadow deliberately seals records no verifier accepts (rollback switch). seal_unchecked_for_tests is a public, doc-hidden bypass of the check that production code must not call; nothing enforces that.

claims.statement: The averin-verify bundle headline word is the report's claim verdict: PASS only when the requested claim is satisfied and the signing keys are externally pinned, CONSISTENT when it is satisfied only under the bundle's own keys, INSUFFICIENT when it is not satisfied or the claims contract is missing or invalid, FAIL when ok is false or the claim is refuted. Exit codes are 0 PASS, 2 CONSISTENT, 1 FAIL or INSUFFICIENT. Held by an end-to-end test of the binary on the shipped fixture (unpinned, pinned, unsatisfied claim, tampered) and by a differential of the Rust verdict function against verifier/claim-verdict.js (run with node) over every case of the committed verdict oracle corpus crossed with every requested claim, ok and pinning, plus malformed contracts.
claims.does_not_establish: That the report's claims are right (that is the claim kernel's refinement and oracle differential). Only the words and exit codes derived from a finished report: the web app's TypeScript copy (web/src/lib/claimVerdict.ts) is covered by its own unit tests, not this differential. The corpus rows are claim decisions, not bundles, so the differential crosses them with synthetic ok and pinning flags rather than verifying real bundles. Usage and unreadable-file errors also exit 2, the same code as CONSISTENT, so a caller must read the RESULT line, not only the exit code. Needs node on PATH. A finite differential, not a proof.

claims.statement: The Level-3 action_completeness label is never stronger than the claim kernel: a brokered capstone label requires the kernel's complete_brokered claim to be satisfied and an introspected label requires complete_introspected, otherwise the label is claimed_over_manifest. Held by a test over every case of the committed verdict oracle corpus (a report is built from each case's checked facts and the shipped label function is applied), by an adversarial test that downgrades a clean capstone report when the kernel is insufficient or refuted, and by the unchanged real-flow capstone tests.
claims.does_not_establish: That the kernel itself is right (see verdict-kernel-refinement). That a label is granted whenever the kernel is satisfied: the cap only removes labels, the legacy conjunction still decides whether one is granted. The corpus test builds each report from checked facts by an inverse projection written in the test, not from real bundles, so a field the projection sets differently from verify.rs could hide or invent a case. The introspected label was not stronger than the kernel on any corpus case, so its cap is exercised only by the adversarial test. Not a proof: a finite corpus.
